findings.citation: P. Sikivie, Q. Yang, "Bose-Einstein Condensation of Dark Matter Axions", Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 111301 (2009), arXiv:0901.1106
findings.summary: Argues that cold dark-matter axions are driven by their own gravitational interaction to thermalize and Bose-condense: (almost) all axions go into one quantum state, with condensate patches about the size of the horizon, so the axions collect in one state while staying spread through space. In a homogeneous universe that state is the lowest momentum mode, which is condensation in momentum space in Einstein's sense. Continued rethermalization puts infalling axions into the lowest-energy state at fixed angular momentum (net rotation), which the authors use to explain caustic rings; the full treatment is Erken, Sikivie, Tam and Yang, Phys. Rev. D 85, 063520 (2012), arXiv:1111.1157. It is the closest published statement that dark matter collects collectively in momentum space through its own attraction.
findings.difference: Ordinary gravity plus Bose degeneracy drives the condensation; there is no attraction gated in relative velocity, no conjugate (p-polarized) sector and no Born reciprocity. The outcome is one condensate in the lowest-energy state, not a smooth Maxwellian fragmenting into a few discrete streams at different mean velocities. It holds only for highly degenerate bosons, the same requirement the record's classicality theorem reaches (#11 §9 (i)). The paper does not use the words 'momentum space'; equating Bose condensation with momentum-space clumping is the textbook reading and the notebook's own ('below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses — momentum-space clumping, realized', #1 §5.2). Its long-range coherence is disputed by Guth, Hertzberg and Prescod-Weinstein 2015 (evidence-against below). Citation graph: the 562 citing papers filtered for 'momentum space', 'velocity space', 'discrete flows' and 'condensation in momentum space' contain no statement of velocity-space fragmentation; the 35 references are the axion and BEC-halo lineage (Sin 1992/94, Böhmer–Harko 2007, Semikoz–Tkachev 1995).

quotes.text: We show that cold dark matter axions thermalize and form a Bose-Einstein condensate.
Axion BEC means that (almost) all axions go to one state.
Thus gravitational interactions cause the axions to thermalize and form a BEC
We expect overlapping condensate patches with typical size of order the horizon.

findings.citation: L. Berezhiani, J. Khoury, "Theory of dark matter superfluidity", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103510 (2015), arXiv:1507.01019
findings.summary: Dark matter made of eV-mass axion-like particles with strong self-interactions condenses into a superfluid core inside galaxies, where the velocity dispersion (and so the temperature) is low; in clusters, where the dispersion is higher, it is partly or wholly in the normal phase. In the condensed phase the dark matter behaves as collective excitations rather than individual collisionless particles. This is the notebook's form of C6, 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses', with 'superfluid-like cores in dwarfs' (#1 §5.2), and the same split between galaxies and clusters as the program's knee.
findings.difference: The condensate is a Bose–Einstein superfluid produced by strong contact self-interactions and Bose degeneracy, not by an attraction gated in relative velocity; there is one condensate, not several velocity streams; the aim is MOND phenomenology through phonons coupled to baryons; nothing is conjugate or momentum-polarized. Citation graph: forward citations filtered for 'momentum space' or 'velocity space' with 'condens' gave one unrelated thesis; the references are the BEC-halo lineage (Sin, Ji–Sin, Böhmer–Harko, Sikivie–Yang, Guth–Hertzberg–Prescod-Weinstein).

quotes.text: The condensate has a polytropic equation of state P~rho^3 giving rise to a superfluid core within galaxies.
due to the higher velocity dispersion in clusters, and correspondingly higher temperature, the DM in clusters is either in a mixture of superfluid and normal phase, or fully in the normal phase
Instead of behaving as individual collisionless particles, the DM superfluid is more aptly described as collective excitations.

findings.citation: A. H. Guth, M. P. Hertzberg, C. Prescod-Weinstein, "Do Dark Matter Axions Form a Condensate with Long-Range Correlation?", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103513 (2015), arXiv:1412.5930
findings.summary: Examines the Sikivie–Yang claim and argues that thermalization through attractive interactions (gravity, attractive self-coupling) produces localized Bose clumps (stars, solitons) with only short-range correlation; only repulsive interactions drive long-range order. A condensate forms, but it is not coherent over cosmological distances.
findings.difference: Weighs against the gravity-driven route to a condensate that is localized in momentum and spread through space, the published form closest to C6. It concerns attraction in position; it does not treat an attraction gated in velocity, whose Born-dual reading would localize in momentum rather than position, so it is not a test of the record's gated model.

quotes.text: there is an essential difference between the thermalization and formation of a condensate due to repulsive interactions, which can indeed drive long-range order, and that due to attractive interactions, which can lead to localized Bose clumps (stars or solitons) that only exhibit short range correlation
we conclude that while a Bose-Einstein condensate is formed, the claim of long-range correlation is unjustified

findings.citation: D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev, "Gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation in the kinetic regime", Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 151301 (2018), arXiv:1804.05857
findings.summary: Shows with kinetic theory and simulations that light bosonic dark matter in virialized halos and miniclusters Bose-condenses through gravity alone, ending in Bose stars, and gives the condensation time. The record cites it as the method behind its wave-island rate (#11 §9 (ii), 'LPT-style').
findings.difference: Collective condensation by an attractive self-interaction does happen for wave dark matter, but what forms is a lump localized in position (a Bose star), not streams spread through space and localized in velocity. No velocity gate, no conjugate sector.

quotes.text: We study Bose-Einstein condensation and formation of Bose stars in the virialized dark matter halos/miniclusters by universal gravitational interactions.

Ketterle, "Spinor condensates and light scattering from Bose-Einstein condensates", in Coherent atomic matter waves, Les Houches Summer School Session LXXII (1999), Springer (2001), doi:10.1007/3-540-45338-5_2, arXiv:cond-mat/0005001 (book chapter, lecture notes)
findings.summary: States the standard reading of Bose–Einstein condensation as a condensation in momentum space, attributing it to Einstein: in Bragg spectroscopy a trapped condensate stands out from the thermal cloud more sharply in momentum than in position.
findings.difference: Matter collecting in momentum space is textbook physics for degenerate bosons. It needs quantum degeneracy (the record's classicality theorem reaches the same requirement) and no attraction in momentum space. Nothing about dark matter or conjugate matter. It means that what is distinctive in C6 is its mechanism and setting, not the phrase 'matter clumps in momentum space'. The original is London 1938 (not read; see unverified leads).

findings.citation: R. Delbourgo, D. Lashmar, "Born reciprocity and the 1/r potential", Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008), arXiv:0709.0776
findings.summary: Applies Born reciprocity to the 1/r potential: the Hamiltonian H = (p² + b²r²)/2m − α(1/r + b/p) gives the Coulomb or Newton attraction a reciprocal partner −αb/p, an attraction in momentum space. In a galaxy the pair interaction becomes GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|), averaged over all other masses and their relative speeds; with Ω ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ Hz the extra term flattens rotation curves without dark matter. The momentum term changes how velocity follows from momentum (ṙ = p(1/m + bα/p³)), not the force.
findings.difference: This is the Born-reciprocal 'gravity in momentum space' that C6's mechanism needs (#1 §5.2's mean field with an attractive U(p − p′); App. A item 10), used as a mean field over co-moving neighbours in a galaxy. The authors draw no conclusion about matter clumping in momentum space; they use the term in place of dark matter, for ordinary matter. No collective instability, no conjugate polarization, no gate width.

findings.citation: J. G. Burgers, C. L. M. Mantz, T. Prokopec, "The Newtonian Limit of Hermitian Gravity", Gen. Rel. Grav. 45, 155 (2013), arXiv:0912.1517
findings.summary: In Hermitian gravity, a Born-reciprocal extension of general relativity to a complex manifold of space-time and momentum-energy (Mantz and Prokopec 2008), the field of a point mass integrated over positions obeys a momentum-space Laplace equation, ∇ₚ²φₚ ∝ M δ²(p) (eqs. 65–66), solved by a logarithmic potential in momentum: a Newtonian potential in momentum space, which the authors present as a realization of Born's reciprocity.
findings.difference: Gravity acting in momentum space in a Born-reciprocal theory, for a single point source only: no matter distribution, no clumping, no dark matter. The authors also report that this version of the theory misses light deflection by 25%.

findings.citation: C. Castro, "Maximal proper force, black hole horizons and matter as curvature in momentum space", Int. J. Geom. Meth. Mod. Phys. 15, 1850035 (2018), doi:10.1142/S0219887818500354 (not on arXiv)
findings.summary: Working with the geometry of the cotangent bundle (phase space) and a maximal proper force, relates the black-hole horizon radius to a singularity of momentum-space curvature, and suggests that matter stress-energy and vacuum energy may be read as curvature of momentum space.
findings.difference: Momentum-space geometry and momentum-space black holes, without dark matter or any clumping of matter in momentum; a geometric reinterpretation, not a dynamical claim.

findings.citation: C. B. Das, S. Das Gupta, C. Gale, B.-A. Li, "Momentum dependence of symmetry potential in asymmetric nuclear matter for transport model calculations", Phys. Rev. C 67, 034611 (2003), arXiv:nucl-th/0212090
findings.summary: Transport (BUU) models of heavy-ion collisions use a momentum-dependent mean field whose interaction term is ∫∫ f(r,p) f(r,p′)/(1 + (p − p′)²/Λ²) d³p d³p′ (eq. 10), with Λ a range in momentum; it is a simpler stand-in for the Gogny force, whose momentum dependence is two Gaussians in (k − k′). The single-particle potential (eq. 12) contains ∫ d³p′ f(r,p′)/(1 + (p − p′)²/Λ²), a potential set by the momentum distribution of neighbours at the same position. The form goes back to Gale, Bertsch and Das Gupta, Phys. Rev. C 35, 1666 (1987).

The signs of the coefficients were not checked here. It is used for nucleons, with no dark matter and no claim of fragmentation into velocity streams. The notebook calls the structure 'Berry-curvature transport'; the nuclear momentum-dependent mean field is a closer established analogue.

findings.citation: S.-Y. Ha, E. Tadmor, "From particle to kinetic and hydrodynamic descriptions of flocking", Kinetic and Related Models 1, 415 (2008), doi:10.3934/krm.2008.1.415, arXiv:0806.2182
findings.summary: Kinetic (Vlasov-type) theory of the Cucker–Smale flocking model: each particle aligns its velocity with the others', weighted by a kernel in their spatial distance, and the velocity distribution concentrates onto one common bulk velocity ('flocking').
findings.difference: Velocity concentration produced by an interaction is the defining result of flocking theory, the source of the founding image's vocabulary ('flocking', 'murmurations'). The alignment is dissipative rather than a Hamiltonian attraction, is weighted by distance in position rather than gated in velocity, and drives the whole system to one velocity rather than several streams. Not gravity, not dark matter.

findings.citation: S. Alexander, S. Cormack, "Gravitationally bound BCS state as dark matter", JCAP 04 (2017) 005, arXiv:1607.08621
findings.summary: Fermionic dark matter with an attractive interaction (torsion-induced) undergoes a BCS transition; self-consistent superfluid halos are solved together with gravity, and dwarf-sized halos need a particle mass of about 200 eV.
findings.difference: A BCS-paired dark-matter halo exists as a model, matching the notebook's BCS analogy, but the pairing interaction is a contact attraction, not one gated in relative velocity, and the result is a superfluid halo, not velocity streams.

findings.citation: F. Xu, A. M. Wang, X. D. Yang, H. You, "Numerical Simulation Solution of the BCS Pairing Problem", Commun. Theor. Phys. 44, 171 (2005), doi:10.1088/6102/44/1/171, arXiv:quant-ph/0407100
findings.summary: Restates standard BCS theory: the reduced interaction pairs electrons of equal energy and opposite momenta and spins, (k↑, −k↓), and the attraction acts only within a shell of energies near the Fermi surface.
findings.difference: The notebook says 'a momentum-gated attraction is precisely the pairing interaction' (#1 §5.2). In BCS the attraction is restricted to an energy shell and pairs opposite momenta (relative momentum near 2k_F, zero total momentum), whereas an attraction gated to small relative velocity acts on the opposite set of pairs. This weighs against the BCS analogy as stated ('exact in structure'), not against momentum-space clumping. Any BCS textbook gives the same; this paper is the one whose text was checked.

findings.citation: P. Sikivie, I. I. Tkachev, Y. Wang, "The Velocity peaks in the cold dark matter spectrum on earth", Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 2911 (1995), arXiv:astro-ph/9504052
findings.summary: Generalizes the secondary-infall model of halo formation and predicts that the cold dark matter velocity distribution at the Earth has discrete peaks: halo dark matter arrives in a set of discrete flows with distinct velocities. Natarajan and Sikivie, Phys. Rev. D 72, 083513 (2005), argue the discrete flows are robust; Erken et al. 2012 state that in the non-linear regime cold dark matter produces discrete flows.
findings.difference: The velocity structure is inherited from cold initial conditions (dark matter lies on a thin sheet in phase space that folds during infall), not produced by an instability of a smooth distribution under an attraction among co-moving particles. The flows are cold and narrow, not of width ~v*, and no new interaction is involved. It is a prior statement of the observable (dark matter in discrete velocity streams), not of the clumping mechanism.

quotes.text: The cold dark matter spectrum on earth is expected to have peaks in velocity space.

findings.citation: M. Zemp, J. Diemand, M. Kuhlen, P. Madau, B. Moore, D. Potter, J. Stadel, L. Widrow, "The Graininess of Dark Matter Haloes", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 394, 641 (2009), arXiv:0812.2033

It bears on the test the momentum-gravity note proposes (§4: only about ten broad streams would test the image): such streams are expected in outer halos anyway, so a discriminating test would have to look at inner halos or at stream widths.

findings.citation: R. Delbourgo, D. Lashmar, "Born reciprocity and the 1/r potential", Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008), arXiv:0709.0776
findings.summary: Writing Newtonian gravity in Born-reciprocal form, H = (p² + b²r²)/2m − α(1/r + b/p) with α = GMm, the interaction between two masses becomes GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|): beside the 1/r term there is a reciprocal term that does not depend on separation and grows as the relative velocity falls, so bodies moving at similar velocities interact most strongly. Summed over a galaxy's masses and their relative speeds, the term flattens rotation curves without dark matter (Ω ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ Hz); the authors note that it weakens between galaxies receding in the Hubble flow. In the Hamiltonian the term changes how velocity follows from momentum (ṙ = p(1/m + bα/p³)), not the force.
findings.difference: A close variant in a different model: (i) it acts among all masses, as a replacement for dark matter, not among dark-matter particles only; (ii) it is an added term proportional to 1/|v − v′|, with no gate width v* and no dependence on distance, not a 1/r attraction multiplied by a gate W(|v − v′|/v*); (iii) it is non-relativistic and breaks Galilean invariance, which the authors list among their own criticisms; (iv) the authors make no claim about clumping. Its Hamiltonian behaviour is the record's 'Hamiltonian reading' (#1 §5.2; momentum-gravity note §2: 'A potential in momentum differences exerts no force'), and its Hubble remark parallels the note's Hubble-flow gating (§6). The record's null search (review/momentum-gravity/run2/analyses/clumping.json, C18) did not find it. Citation graph: 5 citing papers (Castro 2008, 2009, 2011; Pavsic 2009; Ghosh 2017), none develops the term; the 15 references (Born 1949, Jarvis–Morgan, Low, Govaerts et al., Milgrom) contain no earlier form of it.

findings.citation: M. Costa, C. Creque-Sarbinowski, O. Simon, Z. J. Weiner, "Dark forces suppress structure growth", JCAP 06 (2026) 055, arXiv:2510.00098
findings.summary: Minimal models of scalar-mediated attractive forces between dark-matter particles do not enhance the growth of unbiased tracers: the faster growth of the density contrast is cancelled by faster dilution of the background dark-matter density, and CMB-compatible versions suppress structure growth.
findings.difference: A long-range attraction among dark matter only, but not velocity-gated; its main cosmological effects come through the background (faster dilution of the background dark-matter density), which the gated model lacks. This supports the momentum-gravity note's statement (§6) that the BOSS full-shape bound on scalar forces is set by the background modification and does not transfer to the gated model.

quotes.text: We show that minimal models of scalar-mediated forces between dark matter particles do not enhance the growth of unbiased tracers of structure

findings.citation: M. Kesden, M. Kamionkowski, "Galilean Equivalence for Galactic Dark Matter", Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 131303 (2006), arXiv:astro-ph/0606566
findings.summary: If dark matter feels a stronger self-attraction than baryons, stars gain energy preferentially during tidal disruption and the trailing tidal stream is enhanced; the roughly equal streams of the Sagittarius dwarf challenge differences in acceleration above about 10%.
findings.difference: A bound on an extra long-range attraction among dark matter only, not gated in velocity. For a gated force it applies at the satellite's relative speed; the momentum-gravity note (§6) maps it to ε ≲ O(1) (0.2–2.5) at v* = 120 km/s and finds it weaker than the Lyman-α forest. The record already uses it; listed here because its result weighs against the conjecture's required strength (ε > 1).

quotes.text: The Sgr dwarf galaxy is seen to have roughly equal streams, challenging models in which DM and baryons accelerate differently by more than 10%.

findings.citation: T.-T. Wang, Y.-G. Ma, Z.-Q. Zhang, "Effects of Ptot gates and velocity gates on light-particle momentum correlation in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions", Phys. Rev. C 99, 054626 (2019), arXiv:1909.06986
findings.summary: 'Velocity gates' and momentum gates are cuts on pair velocity or total pair momentum used to select particle pairs in femtoscopic correlation functions of heavy-ion collisions.
findings.difference: Same words, different thing: an experimental selection cut, not a force switched on by relative velocity. Most INSPIRE hits for 'velocity-gated' are of this kind.

quotes.text: The results indicate that momentum correlation functions gating with total pair momentum is stronger

closest.why: Sikivie and Yang 2009 is the closest published statement that dark matter, through its own attraction, collects collectively in momentum space while staying spread through space (axions Bose-condense by gravity into one state, with horizon-size condensate patches). It differs in mechanism (ordinary gravity plus Bose degeneracy, no velocity gate, no conjugate sector, no Born reciprocity), in outcome (one condensate in the lowest-energy state, not a smooth Maxwellian fragmenting into a few discrete streams of width ~v*), in scope (degenerate bosons only, which the record's classicality theorem also requires), and it never says 'momentum space'. Its long-range coherence is disputed (Guth, Hertzberg and Prescod-Weinstein 2015). For the condensed-core form specifically, Berezhiani and Khoury 2015 (1507.01019) is as close.

For the founding image's mechanism, a Born-reciprocal attraction in momentum space acting as a mean field among co-moving masses (#1 §5.2), the closest paper is Delbourgo and Lashmar 2007: Born reciprocity gives Newtonian gravity a partner term GmMΩ/|v − v′|, averaged over a galaxy's relative speeds. It differs in that it acts among ordinary masses as a replacement for dark matter and draws no conclusion about clumping in momentum space.

Delbourgo and Lashmar 2007 write the pair interaction of two masses as GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|): a Born-reciprocal term, independent of distance, strongest for bodies with similar velocities, applied to galaxy rotation, with a remark that it fades for galaxies receding in the Hubble flow. It differs from C7 in acting among all masses (as an alternative to dark matter) rather than among dark matter only; in being an added 1/|Δv| term with no gate width and no 1/r factor, rather than a 1/r attraction multiplied by a gate W(|v − v′|/v*); in being non-relativistic and not Galilean invariant; and in making no clumping claim. Its Hamiltonian form changes the velocity–momentum relation, as the record's Hamiltonian reading does.

not_found.statement: No paper found that states that dark matter (or any matter) clumps collectively in momentum space by the Jeans mechanism with position and velocity exchanged: that an attraction acting between particles of similar velocity makes a smooth Maxwellian fragment into a few discrete velocity streams spread through space; nor any paper proposing that dark matter is matter of the conjugate (momentum) polarization that clumps in momentum space as ordinary matter clumps in position space. Momentum-space condensation of dark matter appears in print only as Bose–Einstein condensation or superfluidity (one state, degenerate bosons: Sikivie–Yang, Berezhiani–Khoury, Levkov et al.); discrete velocity flows only from cold infall or accretion (Sikivie et al., Zemp et al.); velocity concentration by an interaction only in flocking models (Ha–Tadmor); and a Born-reciprocal momentum-space attraction only without a clumping claim (Delbourgo–Lashmar, Burgers–Mantz–Prokopec).

not_found.statement: No paper found that proposes a long-range (1/r, gravity-like) attraction among dark-matter particles that acts only between particles moving at similar velocities, i.e. a relative-velocity gate W(|v − v′|/v*) on a gravity-like force, whether as dark-matter physics or as a modification of gravity. The closest are Delbourgo–Lashmar's Born-reciprocal term GmMΩ/|v − v′| among all masses (partial), the velocity-dependent correction of continuous-spin forces (Schuster–Toro–Zhou; scalar, threshold falling with distance), the Hatsugai–Kohmoto momentum-local interaction of infinite range (lattice electrons), and velocity-dependent self-interactions, which are collisional. This confirms and extends the record's earlier null search (review/momentum-gravity/run2/analyses/clumping.json, C18), which had missed Delbourgo–Lashmar.

notes: Group g5 (C6, C7). No paper anticipates either conjecture. C6: two partials. Sikivie–Yang 2009: dark matter Bose-condenses by its own gravity into one state, coherent over horizon-size patches. Berezhiani–Khoury 2015: halo cores condense into a superfluid below a critical velocity dispersion, clusters stay normal. Both are Bose condensation of degenerate bosons, which the record's classicality theorem also says collective momentum-space behaviour requires; neither has a velocity-gated attraction, velocity streams or a conjugate sector. Guth–Hertzberg–Prescod-Weinstein 2015 weighs against the gravity-driven form (attraction gives position-space clumps, not long-range order).
